claim: The charter demands a "verified disposition of f-060..f-073" but never defines what verification requires, who performs it, or what vocabulary a disposition is written in — so a downstream run can restate each finding's own self-attestation as confirmation and build the entire ranking on an unchecked frontier.
evidence: The source synthesis anticipates exactly this and the charter does not close it — 2026-08-24-synthesis.md Caveat 1: "Each carries a lens self-attestation ('VERIFIED on the trace' with file:line), and I spot-checked the file/line citations for internal consistency, but none received independent adjudication." Every record f-060..f-073 in heat-ledger.jsonl carries "status": "raw" and a null `lens` field, so a verifier cannot even identify the filing party. The only nearby discipline clause, :26 ("Treat these as claims to verify or bound, not axioms"), governs the four inherited conclusions, not the finding-level check, and names no standard. Re-reading internal/agentloop/autocompact.go:149 because f-070 says to reproduces the filing lens's own check; f-070's consequence (any in-band grade fails the epistemic gate mechanically) is what needs adjudication and nothing asks for it.

claim: Four of the five policy claimants the charter orders ranked inherit a refuted or explicitly unrepaired premise, and the per-candidate obligation list never requires that dependency be surfaced — so a shortlisted candidate is scored on enforceability using a mechanism the prior run already adjudicated non-functional.
evidence: Stint's origin f-067 repairs the refuted f-052, whose mechanism was GateConstraint.RateLimit — broken in the running system: internal/tool/registry.go:116 documents ResetRateCounts as "call on phase transition" and it has zero production callers (only reference outside the definition is internal/tool/registry_test.go:484), so every RateLimit is a per-process-lifetime budget. Season's origin f-057 asserts in field 7 that ResetRateCounts zeroes on phase transition; the synthesis rules it "resolved against f-057" and states "its runtime-delta half must be re-derived before scoring." Fallow (f-063) is buildable only because f-004 was refuted (Caveat 8); Divert's origin is f-034 with f-001 refuted. Failure: step 4 scores Season on "enforceability in an agent harness" (:61) via a dead counter, and the implementer ships a cohort rate limit whose "N probes per S visit" stop rule silently becomes N per process.

claim: Nothing forbids ranking or recommending a candidate whose origin finding is still status: raw, and the :30 priority list omits the three findings that carry two policy claimants' contracts and the clustering rule the synthesis recommends adopting — so the ranking runs on findings the charter itself deprioritized.
evidence: All of f-060..f-073 are `status: raw` in heat-ledger.jsonl. The prioritized four (f-063, f-064, f-066, f-070) omit f-067 (Stint's contract), f-071 (Slacken's contract) and f-072 — which the synthesis §3 explicitly recommends adopting into Required-output item 1 ("the survival test as a clustering rule ... Adopt it"). Required output 1 (verified disposition) can be satisfied after item 5 (policy-class ranking) without contradicting any clause. Failure: the run verifies the prioritized four, ranks Fallow first and Slacken second on f-071's compaction-covariate argument, and never checks f-071 — which the ledger scores at likelihood 2, the least confident of the round-3 policy findings.

claim: The Stress-test and Simulate/Sweep repairs are stated as decisions with no discriminating test named, against an equivalence key the prior run proved incomplete in exactly the dimension that separates them — so the answer is settled by whichever framing the reviewer writes first and cannot be reproduced or reversed.
evidence: Two usable predicates exist in the sources and the charter names neither: v2 charter lesson 6 at docs/research/2026-08-24-oodarcs-s-phase-tournament-v2.md:42 ("Cluster synonyms unless their contracts, triggers, outputs, or authority differ") and f-072's persistence rule ("what crosses Skaffen's compaction boundary is only {first 200 chars of goal, ≤10 read/write/edit paths, phase string} ... same persistence ⇒ same candidate"). The synthesis records the key as known incomplete: f-045 ("the clustering predicate merges on contract/trigger/output/authority but never on spend, so a cheap screen and a costly dispositive test collapse into one candidate before scoring") and f-059 (omits issuing authority). Simulate-vs-Sweep is precisely a spend distinction — Sweep reuses internal/experiment's ExpandMutations capped at 24 permutations, a costly dispositive run.

claim: Thirteen contradictions were open when the source run halted and the charter requires disposition of none of them, including D1 — the disagreement that decides whether the remedy class most of the field relies on is void.

D3 (which candidate occupies the policy slot) is correctly inherited as charter step 4; D6 (Season's pre-committed rate vs Stint's adaptive) sits inside step 4 unnamed; D1 ("Can epistemic separation be carried in-band at all?" — f-070 vs f-043/f-058, "the highest-stakes open disagreement in the run") is imported only as the flattened assertion at :26; D4 (is Compound thin or the most dangerous write in the system) and D7 (Frontier: spend economy or mint accelerant) have no home at all, and D4 makes Compound itself a claimant on the subtraction verdict. Failure: a run satisfies every numbered output while D1 stays open and the first-implementation verdict recommends a contract whose field-4 answer is "carries a grade" — the exact class f-070 invalidates.

claim: The charter re-imports the hard gate the prior run proved ranks candidates in inverse order of governability, adds no governability criterion and none of the named repair, and then makes the emit-nothing class the subject of its only mandated ranking — so the matrix orders the field inversely to the property the design most needs.
evidence: Synthesis §1, f-042 (heat 27, required fusion 1): "The epistemic-separation hard gate grades products, so a candidate whose output is an allocation change clears it by emitting nothing — the gate ranks candidates in inverse order of governability. Fix: the Warrant contract plus a fourth gate clause." :35 imports the gates by reference without the fourth clause; criterion 2 at :57 restates the same product-shaped test as a score; no criterion in :56-65 asks who authorized a spend or whether a lapsed licence is readable. :36 then ranks five candidates defined by not emitting (Fallow's "entire output is an allocation change and a single number"; Stint's "only output is a held allocation"; Slacken is clock-only), and :37's strongest-survivor-per-class step propagates the class winner rather than correcting the inversion. The inversion is live in this codebase: shouldEscalate() converts ungraded counters into a model upgrade and internal/router/costrouter.go:74-75 calls tracker.reset() at the moment of escalation, destroying the authorizing estimate. Counterweight check: :26 concerns the carrier, not emitting nothing; :76's "failure/Goodhart mode" is narrative and never enters a score.

claim: "Qualitative ratings with explicit uncertainty" names no rating vocabulary, no confidence vocabulary, no rule combining a strong rating with weak confidence, no rule for what a cell means when the origin finding is raw, and no tie-break — so the five-way policy ranking the charter mandates is underdetermined.
evidence: A working precedent exists in the source run and is not reused: heat-ledger.jsonl scores novelty 0-3 and risk as {blast_radius, likelihood, product}, and the synthesis moves scores on the record with reasons ("I moved f-031's novelty 3→2"; "I raised f-044's likelihood 2→3 because the default is in the code"). Simulating the framework on three claimants against :65: Fallow — high marginal value, origin f-063 raw, likelihood 2, buildability contingent on f-004's refutation; Stint — moderate value, origin f-067 raw, likelihood 2, predecessor f-052 refuted; Slacken — high value on f-071, raw, likelihood 2. All three write as "high/uncertain" or "moderate/confident" and no clause orders them. Failure: two reviewers on identical verified findings produce different policy rankings — one leads with Fallow on value, one with Stint on confidence — and neither violates a clause.

claim: The three verdicts are declared separable with no rule linking them to the shortlist, the ranking, or the pilots — so a run can satisfy required outputs 5, 6 and 7 simultaneously while recommending one candidate, ranking a field that excludes it, and piloting two others.

Failure: the implementer receives a recommendation to build Reprove first, backed by pilots that measured Fallow and Survey and a ranking over five candidates none of which is Reprove — three internally valid artifacts that jointly justify nothing, and no reversal condition attaches to the recommended candidate because it was never piloted.

claim: "Marginal value over no-S" is the aggregate of the other nine criteria against a particular comparator, yet is scored as a tenth column — double-weighting the same evidence — and "cognitive and implementation cost" fuses a dimension the charter separately demands be exercised explicitly with the one that already has evidence.
evidence: Synthesis Caveat 7 records the asymmetry that makes the bundle harmful: "the human-factors/cognitive-load position (the charter's 'cognitive cost' criterion at :113 was scored by nobody)" — while implementation cost was scored throughout (f-063 "with zero new instrumentation"; f-066's "one-hunk fix"). On the double-count: :36 frames the whole policy ranking as "against each other and no-S", :65 scores it again, and proposition 6 at :86 tests the null a third time, with no statement of which is the scoring one. Failure over weeks: Fallow — whose defining property is its relation to the null — collects credit on generativity, falsification, marginal value, the :36 framing and proposition 6 from a single argument, and the ordering looks like convergent evidence.

claim: Reversal conditions are required of the recommendation but never required to be observable in the pilots the same charter specifies, so the recommendation can ship with criteria no planned measurement could trip.
evidence: The source run supplies both poles. Measurable: f-063's losing condition — "if spontaneous exploration already meets the proposed quota, :43 resolves for the null and takes every S candidate with it" — countable "from existing evidence tool_calls with zero new instrumentation." Failure: required output 9 ships three reversal conditions, two of which read on channels that record nothing; the design is never reversed and the absence of contrary evidence is read as confirmation.

claim: "Identical budgets" names no currency; in this runtime the currency is a config field whose default ignores exactly the cached context the treatment arms differ by, so equal budget silently subsidizes or taxes the treatment arm and every headline comparison is uninterpretable regardless of outcome.
evidence: Verified in the repo: internal/router/config.go:25 — `Tracking string `json:"tracking"` // "billing" (default), "context"`; internal/router/budget_test.go:150-166 confirms an unset field reports billing; budget_test.go:140-142 states "billing mode: only 100 + 100 = 200 (cache tokens ignored)". The prior run filed this as f-044 and the synthesis raised its likelihood 2→3 "because the default is in the code." The charter's :26 acknowledges the pilot is confounded but its only repair step (:31-34) is scoped to the field (Stress-test, Simulate), not the pilot; :40 is the sole pilot clause and names no currency. Failure: the Fallow/no-S pilot runs at "equal budget", the null arm burns its allowance on Orient's per-turn re-strike while Fallow's withheld tasking leaves cached context uncharged, Fallow posts a better turns-to-useful-probe number, and nobody can tell from the artifact which way the subsidy ran.

claim: "Identical stores" is satisfied by the arms sharing one store, and in this runtime sharing is the only reachable configuration — so the incumbent Orient read path feeds each arm the other arm's rows and a null result becomes indistinguishable from contamination.
evidence: cmd/skaffen/main.go:290 and :526 — mutations.NewStore(filepath.Join(cfg.UserDir(), "mutations")); internal/config/config.go:34 — userDir: filepath.Join(home, ".skaffen") from os.UserHomeDir(); there is no environment override for the store or evidence directory (the only os.Getenv calls in cmd/skaffen/main.go are ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at :659, :677, :704). claim: The "distinct runtime phase now" verdict is demanded with no stated operational test, in a runtime that does not agree with itself about what the phase list is — the FSM holds six phases and the TUI holds five.

claim: No clause requires a pilot arm to name what fires its treatment, and for the pairing the charter privileges nothing in the runtime can fire one of them — Survey is defined as untriggered fixed-cadence sampling in a system whose only phase entry is a human keystroke.
evidence: The sole caller of Advance() is the /advance command at internal/tui/commands.go:196; there is no scheduler, timer, or cross-session cadence anywhere in the tree. Survey (f-064) samples "on a fixed cadence against a frame chosen independently of any trigger", and the synthesis states "Skaffen has no untriggered cross-session scheduler at all." Fallow is the mirror case and is fine — withholding needs no trigger. Failure: the Survey arm degrades to "the operator remembers to run a sampling session", making cadence a function of operator attention — the exact variable Fallow exists to measure — and collapsing the 2×2: a "Survey zero" cell cannot be distinguished from "the human did not run Survey this week", so the identification claim :36 conditions the pairing on fails on the trigger rather than on the statistics.

claim: Multi-agent/topology coherence is required both as a scored criterion and as a neglected dimension to exercise, but nothing in the harness makes multi-agent interaction observable — so the cell will be filled with unfalsifiable prose carrying the same weight as code-verified criteria.

But one concrete multi-instance surface does exist: the shared user-global store at ~/.skaffen/mutations (cmd/skaffen/main.go:290, internal/config/config.go:34) plus the context-file channel f-050 identified — Compound's manifest-globbed write (manifestGlobs includes "*.md" at internal/tool/registry.go:44-46) lands in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, prepended to every future session's system prompt at top precedence. Two instances on one machine interact through both, unarbitrated. Failure over weeks: the topology row differentiates nobody, contributes weight to whichever advocate wrote more confidently, and the one real risk — a second instance reading the first's ungraded speculative material at top precedence — is never tested.

claim: Adjudication of the disputed pair: the dial claim (f-017) holds and dominates; the underdetermination claim (f-007) is real but strictly subordinate, and fixing it first makes the defect worse. Sharpened, the dial claim is that requirement 4 enters the no-S null's own measurement instrument (Fallow) into the field as a rival to the null it measures — four of five rows are settings of one control variable (the exploration quota) differing only in entry rule, the fifth (Slacken) is a different control surface. Since every value criterion at :54-65 is a declared tie and only cost-to-instrument can be ordered, and Fallow is by construction the cheapest, the winner is foreordained before any rating vocabulary is chosen; supplying that vocabulary launders 'the dial's off-position is cheapest to instrument' into a crisp total order that then feeds requirement 8's top-two and the first-implementation verdict at :48.
intersection_justification: Fuses the two disputed findings — the underdetermination lens (no rating/confidence vocabulary, combination rule, tie-break) and the dial-collapse lens (Fallow/Stint/Season are settings of one call). Their intersection is what neither states alone: the two defects are anti-aligned, because a well-specified procedure applied to a pre-decided object produces a laundered verdict instead of a visibly soft one. Demoted to convergence: parent lens fd-changeringing-method-truth already filed this location+cause as f-017.

claim: The subtractive class's entire safety claim — Melt's 'deface, never os.Remove' — is a reversibility claim the runtime does not support: the only production commit path fires when a human types /commit in the TUI, and headless mode has no git at all, so a Reprove/Melt firing destroys durable knowledge with no recoverable prior state. Nothing in the charter's adversarial obligations or criteria ever asks a candidate what it writes to or what preserves the prior state.

claim: Skaffen has two compaction clocks with different discard laws — a positional loop clock in both modes and a mutation-scored, phase-biased TUI-only clock — and requirement 8's "identical … compaction treatment" controls neither the trigger nor the selection law, both of which are endogenous to the treatment and anti-correlated with every S candidate's product.

evidence: Clock 1 (both modes): fires at `effectiveWindow - 13000` before each LLM call (loop.go:147-149), discards positionally — microCompact stubs oldest tool results (autocompact.go:135), snip drops oldest outside a 6-message tail (autocompact.go:194). Exploration output is exactly the 2.0-4.0 band; edits are 8.0-10.0, so the TUI clock deletes the exploring arm's evidence and preserves the exploiting arm's. Headless print mode never builds a TUI (main.go:99-105,:208), so clock 2 and the scoring never run — a headless pilot measures positional truncation while the shipped design would live under mutation-scored retention, and :40 never names execution mode. The two clocks' denominators disagree (fixed 200k vs `router.ContextWindow(model)`), so which discard law fires first can flip by phase. Remediation: amend requirement 8 to fix and declare a single execution mode for every arm and require per-arm logging of both compaction paths (loop snip/microCompact counts and, in TUI mode, ScoreMessages retention bucketed by tool class).
